title: Karnataka Cabinet Approves AI Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur
excerpt: The state government allocated Rs 5 crore as part of the 2026-27 budget to establish an AI research hub at the Indian Institute of Information Technology in Raichur
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Karnataka allocated Rs 5 crore for an AI Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur in the 2026-27 budget.
  • The initiative is part of a broader AI strategy, including a robotics hub in Bengaluru.
  • IIIT Raichur aims to foster regional development through its AI-focused programs.
  • Karnataka plans AI tutoring for 12.28 lakh students and a government-driven AI university.
  • The state targets 500 new Global Capability Centres by 2029, creating 3.5 lakh jobs.

  • Karnataka allocated Rs 5 crore to set up a Centre of Excellence for AI at IIIT Raichur as part of the 2026-27 state budget
  • The announcement was part of a broader AI push that includes a robotics hub in Bengaluru with IISc and ISRO, and a surgical robot partnership with IIIT-Bangalore and NIMHANS
  • IIIT Raichur is already building a Centre of Excellence in AI for Innovation and Entrepreneurship focused on regional development
  • Karnataka also announced AI-based tutoring for 12.28 lakh students and plans for India's first government-driven AI university

The Karnataka government has approved the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Artificial Intelligence at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Raichur, with an investment of Rs 5 crore announced as part of the state's 2026-27 budget.

Chief Minister Siddaramaiah made the announcement while presenting the Rs 4.48 lakh crore state budget in the Vidhana Soudha on March 6, 2026 — his historic 17th budget presentation.

Part of a Broader AI Strategy

The IIIT Raichur centre is one piece of an ambitious AI agenda unveiled in the Karnataka budget. The state also announced the establishment of a "Bangalore Robotics and AI Innovation Zone," to be set up by the AI and Robotics Technology Park at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in partnership with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Limited (KEONICS).

Additionally, Rs 4 crore was earmarked for developing an advanced surgical-assisted robot (COBOT) through a collaboration between IIIT-Bangalore and NIMHANS, aimed at improving outcomes in neurosurgical operations.

"This policy aims to set up 500 new GCCs in the state by 2029, projected to provide jobs for 3.5 lakh individuals and yield an economic output of USD 50 billion." — Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, during the budget speech

Why IIIT Raichur Matters

IIIT Raichur was established in 2019 under the Government of India's public-private partnership model and currently offers B.Tech programmes in Computer Science and Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, and Mathematics and Computing. The institute is already in the process of building a Centre of Excellence in AI for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, with a focus on regional development in the Kalyana-Karnataka region.

The state's decision to locate an AI centre in Raichur — a district in northern Karnataka historically associated with agriculture rather than technology — signals an effort to distribute tech infrastructure beyond the Bengaluru corridor. This aligns with Siddaramaiah's broader push to develop Mysuru as the state's second IT city and establish new IT parks in Mangalore.

AI Across Education and Governance

The budget also introduced several AI-driven education initiatives. In collaboration with IIT Dharwad, the government plans to deploy an AI-based personalised digital tutor for approximately 12.28 lakh students in Classes 8 to 12, at an estimated cost of Rs 5 crore. Modern AI Data Labs will be set up in 50 government colleges across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities with a Rs 10 crore grant, in collaboration with the Central Government's AI Mission.

An AI-based facial recognition attendance system is also slated for introduction across schools, colleges, and hostels statewide.

Separately, in July 2026, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced that Karnataka will establish India's first government-driven AI University, along with an AI Hub for incubation, research, and development by startups and companies.

Karnataka's Deep Tech Ecosystem

Karnataka has been steadily expanding its AI and deep tech footprint. In January 2026, the state approved a Rs 20 crore Centre of Excellence for AI in Biotechnology at the Institute of Bioinformatics and Applied Biotechnology (IBAB) in Electronic City, Bengaluru, in partnership with the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP). The state also installed a 25-qubit quantum computing system at both IIIT-Dharwad and IIIT-Raichur under its LEAP initiative.

IT Minister Priyank Kharge has described this period as "Karnataka's deep tech decade," emphasising the state's goal of building a pipeline from research to market-ready innovation.

Diaspora Interest

These developments are closely tracked by the Indian technology diaspora, particularly professionals in AI and machine learning roles across Silicon Valley, Seattle, and other global tech hubs. Karnataka contributes nearly 40 percent of India's software exports, and many diaspora professionals maintain active connections to Bengaluru's startup and research ecosystem. The expansion of AI infrastructure to smaller cities like Raichur could create new opportunities for diaspora-led investment and academic collaboration.

What's Next

The IIIT Raichur AI centre is expected to begin operations as the institute moves into its permanent campus. With over 550 Global Capability Centres already operating in the state and a target of 500 more by 2029, Karnataka is positioning itself as the anchor state for India's AI ambitions — with an emphasis on ensuring those ambitions extend beyond Bengaluru's city limits.
